I've attached Crime data for 33 London boroughs and a list showing which boroughs are geographic neighbors of each other.
 
Question: Is Westminster a spatial outlier for Crime -- meaning its value is unusually different from what would be expected given its neighbors' values, once you account for the citywide relationship between a borough's value and its neighborhood's average?
 
Use the ITERATIVE-R method (Lu, Chen & Kou, 2003) -- this is more rigorous than a simple neighbor-difference z-test, and requires ALL of these exact steps, in order:
1. For every borough, compute its own value and its neighbors' average value (the spatial lag).
2. Fit an OLS regression: own_value ~ neighbor_avg, using ALL 33 boroughs (pass 1).
3. Compute residuals, standardize into z-scores.
4. Flag any borough with |z| > 1.96 in pass 1 as a CANDIDATE to exclude.
5. Refit the SAME regression, this time EXCLUDING those candidates -- this corrects for a known bias called 'masking', where an extreme borough can distort the very line used to judge it.
6. Apply this refined line to ALL 33 boroughs (including the excluded candidates) to get final predicted values and residuals.
7. Standardize the final residuals into z-scores. Do NOT skip step 5 -- fitting only once, on all boroughs including outliers, is a materially different (and weaker) method.
 
Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- implement this directly using only pandas and numpy.
 
Focus your final answer specifically on Westminster -- report its OWN final z-score (after the refit in step 6-7), not any other borough's.

or

or

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, os, json, math, sys, itertools

# Paths (ADJACENCY_PATH is already defined in the environment)
CRIME_PATH = "chunks_csv/outlierr/2023_crime.csv"

# 1. Load data
df = pd.read_csv(CRIME_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Standardise column names we need
df.columns = [c.strip().lower() for c in df.columns]
if 'crime_rate' not in df.columns:
    # assume the 2nd column is the numeric value if not explicitly named
    value_col = df.columns[1]
else:
    value_col = 'crime_rate'

# Build borough -> value dictionary
values = dict(zip(df['borough'], df[value_col]))

# Build symmetric neighbour list
if 'neighbor' in adj.columns:
    # long form: one row per pair
    neighbor_map = {}
    for _, row in adj.iterrows():
        b, n = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
        neighbor_map.setdefault(b, []).append(n)
        neighbor_map.setdefault(n, []).append(b)
else:
    # wide form: one row, borough with comma-separated neighbours
    neigh_col = [c for c in adj.columns if c != 'borough'][0]
    neighbor_map = {row['borough']: [x.strip() for x in str(row[neigh_col]).split(',') if x.strip()]
                    for _, row in adj.iterrows()}

# 1. Compute spatial lag (average of neighbours' values)
lags = {}
for b in values:
    neighs = [n for n in neighbor_map.get(b, []) if n in values]
    lags[b] = np.mean([values[n] for n in neighs]) if neighs else np.nan

data = pd.DataFrame({'borough': list(values.keys()),
                     'value': [values[b] for b in values],
                     'lag':   [lags[b]   for b in values]})

# 2. First OLS (pass-1) : value ~ lag  (include intercept)
X1 = np.column_stack((np.ones(len(data)), data['lag'].values))
beta1 = np.linalg.lstsq(X1, data['value'].values, rcond=None)[0]
pred1 = X1 @ beta1
resid1 = data['value'].values - pred1
std1 = resid1.std(ddof=2)
z1 = resid1 / std1
data['z1'] = z1

# 4. Identify candidate outliers (|z| > 1.96)
candidates = data.loc[data['z1'].abs() > 1.96, 'borough'].tolist()

# 5. Refit OLS excluding candidates
mask_keep = ~data['borough'].isin(candidates)
X2 = np.column_stack((np.ones(mask_keep.sum()), data.loc[mask_keep, 'lag'].values))
beta2 = np.linalg.lstsq(X2, data.loc[mask_keep, 'value'].values, rcond=None)[0]

# 6. Apply refined line to all boroughs
pred2_all = np.column_stack((np.ones(len(data)), data['lag'].values)) @ beta2
resid2_all = data['value'].values - pred2_all

# 7. Final standardized residuals
std2 = resid2_all.std(ddof=2)
data['z_final'] = resid2_all / std2

westminster_z = float(data.loc[data['borough'].str.lower() == 'westminster', 'z_final'])
print("Westminster final z-score:", westminster_z)

# 1. Load data
df = pd.read_csv(CRIME_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Standardise column names

if 'crime_rate' not in df.columns:
    value_col = df.columns[1]

    value_col = 'crime_rate'

# Borough -> value

# Build symmetric neighbour list
if 'neighbor' in adj.columns:
    neighbor_map = {}
    for _, row in adj.iterrows():
        b, n = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
        neighbor_map.setdefault(b, []).append(n)
        neighbor_map.setdefault(n, []).append(b)
else:
    neigh_col = [c for c in adj.columns if c != 'borough'][0]
    neighbor_map = {row['borough']: [x.strip() for x in str(row[neigh_col]).split(',') if x.strip()]
                    for _, row in adj.iterrows()}

# 1. Compute spatial lag (average of neighbours' values)
lags = {}
for b in values:
    neighs = [n for n in neighbor_map.get(b, []) if n in values]
    lags[b] = np.mean([values[n] for n in neighs]) if neighs else np.nan

data = pd.DataFrame({
    'borough': list(values.keys()),
    'value':   [values[b] for b in values],
    'lag':     [lags[b]   for b in values]
})

# 2. Pass-1 regression value ~ lag
X1 = np.column_stack((np.ones(len(data)), data['lag'].values))
beta1 = np.linalg.lstsq(X1, data['value'].values, rcond=None)[0]
pred1 = X1 @ beta1
resid1 = data['value'].values - pred1
std1  = resid1.std(ddof=2)
data['z1'] = resid1 / std1

# 4. Candidate exclusions
candidates = data.loc[data['z1'].abs() > 1.96, 'borough'].tolist()

# 5. Refit excluding candidates
keep_mask = ~data['borough'].isin(candidates)
X2 = np.column_stack((np.ones(keep_mask.sum()), data.loc[keep_mask, 'lag'].values))
beta2 = np.linalg.lstsq(X2, data.loc[keep_mask, 'value'].values, rcond=None)[0]

# 6. Apply refined model to ALL boroughs
pred2_all = np.column_stack((np.ones(len(data)), data['lag'].values)) @ beta2
resid2_all = data['value'].values - pred2_all

# 7. Final z-scores
std2 = resid2_all.std(ddof=2)
data['z_final'] = resid2_all / std2

# Westminster result
westminster_z_series = data.loc[data['borough'].str.lower() == 'westminster', 'z_final']
westminster_z = westminster_z_series.iloc[0] if not westminster_z_series.empty else np.nan

print("Candidates excluded in refit:", candidates)
print("Westminster final z-score:", westminster_z)
